summary: Summation No. 16 covers January 1947 in the U.S. Army Military Government in Korea (South Korea), issued by Commander-in-Chief Far East. The month is dominated by politics: the exchange of letters between General Hodge and the Soviet commander over reopening the Joint Commission, Kim Koo's anti-trusteeship movement, the Interim Legislative Assembly's 44-1 resolution against trusteeship of 20 January, and Hodge's public rejoinders. Acting Military Governor Lerch's 9 January address to the Assembly sets out finance, food, industry and reorganization problems. Other reports: reorganization of the National Economic Board, Ordinance No. 128 raising land taxes, suspension of the Child Labor Ordinance, Bank of Chosen note circulation of 18.28 billion yen, rice collection at 78 percent of quota, smallpox, typhus and typhoid outbreaks, refugee relief, repatriation figures and the Korean National Youth Movement. Statistical tables on industry, trade, prices and public health make it useful for economic and political history of the occupation.
highlights: On 11 January Hodge published his exchange of letters with the Soviet commander on reopening the Joint Commission, offering that signing Communique No. 5 would count as good faith toward the Moscow Decision; Kim Koo's anti-trusteeship movement formed in response.

On 20 January the Korean Interim Legislative Assembly passed an anti-trusteeship resolution 44 to 1 with nine abstentions, rejecting an amendment 17 to 43; Hodge replied on 25 January that the resolution misstated the U.S. position.

On 9 January the Acting Military Governor told the Assembly to draft universal-suffrage election laws by end of February, support the rice collection, and review labor ordinances; a single national budget for fiscal 1947 was promised.
The National Economic Board was reorganized with an American chairman and a Korean deputy chairman, absorbing the Korean Economic Advisory Board; it first met on 29 January.
Ordinance No. 128 (effective 10 January) raised land taxes and service fees; Bank of Chosen notes outstanding reached 18,277,613,497.90 yen on 31 January, up 566,990,248 yen in the month.
The Child Labor Ordinance (No. 112) was suspended until 1 June 1947 to allow Assembly review, while hiring children under 14 stayed prohibited; the National Labor Federation formed on 12 January.
Rice collection reached 78 percent of the 1946 quota by 31 January; 69,417 metric tons of imported staple food were released in December, and a twice-monthly ration period starts 12 February.
Health reports showed January typhus cases rising to 647 and typhoid to 457; 10,036 Japanese were repatriated from North Korea and 15,283 Koreans awaited evacuation from Japan.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers, title page for Summation No. 16 (January 1947), table of contents of four parts and list of 34 charts and a map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Brief digest of the month: Joint Commission letters, anti-trusteeship movement, Ordinance No. 128, rice collection at 78 percent, new National Labor Federation and Youth Movement.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Summarizes Hodge's 11 January letters, Kim Koo's anti-trusteeship movement, the People's Party reorganization, Acting Military Governor's 9 January address and five new Constabulary and Coast Guard ranks.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Seed cotton down 14 percent, coal stockpiles up, National Labor Federation formed 12 January, notes in circulation 18.28 billion yen, rail fares raised and 78 percent of rice quota collected.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Relief supplies from Koreans in Japan, 10,036 Japanese repatriated from the north, Winter Institute at Seoul National University, Youth Movement with 19,270 members, trusteeship dominating the press.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Political events of January: economic board reorganization, Hodge's policy statements, Joint Commission correspondence, Assembly debates and the trusteeship resolution, plus legislation, police, prisons, fire and security forces.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Reorganized National Economic Board, Hodge's 4 January policy statement, Joint Commission letters, party mergers, Assembly's 44-1 anti-trusteeship vote of 20 January and Hodge's replies; 49 Japanese remain.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: National Economic Board reorganized with American chairman and Korean deputy chairman; first met 29 January on agricultural goals, food shipping and a copper-mining loan.

sections.title: American Policy
sections.summary: Hodge's 4 January statement that the U.S. does not favor a separate southern government and that the Assembly is an interim body without final executive power.

sections.title: U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Soviet letter of 26 November set three consultation conditions; the U.S. reply of 24 December proposed that signing Communique No. 5 count as good faith.

sections.title: Political Activities
sections.summary: Kim Koo's anti-trusteeship committee, rightist merger talk, Coalition Committee criticism, National Independence Front, Democratic People's Front and the People's Party restoration committee.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Assembly reconvened 6 January; Acting Military Governor's 9 January address; amnesty debate; 44-1 anti-trusteeship resolution on 20 January; Hodge's 25 January reply.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: Latest census reported 49 Japanese nationals still living in South Korea.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Ordinance No. 128 land tax increase, Hodge's 16 January warning against demonstrations, police trial board, 3,683 prison staff, 266 fires costing 261 million yen, Coast Guard seizures.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Economic review: 131.9 million pounds of cotton, coal stockpiles of 368,183 tons, industrial shortages, textile output, foreign trade and permits, finance, transport, communications, rice collection and price control.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Cotton at 131,879,359 pounds, 114,000-ton rice increase planned, November fish catch of 9,168 tons, charcoal at 80 percent of quota, December coal output of 21,041 tons, tungsten 182 tons.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Raw material shortages hamper steel, paper and shoes; textile output by 127 factories; Child Labor Ordinance suspended until 1 June; National Labor Federation; 48,703 industrial workers; 100-million-yen river restoration.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Acting Military Governor's 3 January anti-inflation statement, notes at 18.28 billion yen, gold at 2,400 yen, exports via U.S. Commercial Company, ore exports to Japan, rail fare rise, mail service extended to all countries.

sections.title: Finance and Property Control
sections.summary: Inflation measures, 566,990,248-yen note increase, gold price up 17 percent, International Fire Reinsurance Company licensed 10 January with 20 million yen capital.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: U.S. Commercial Company to sell Korean exports abroad; December permits worth 71.8 million yen; ore exports of 33.8 million yen to Japan; itemized 1946 and January imports.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Passenger rail rate raised to 1 yen per kilometer on 15 January, gasoline shortage, 116 marine disasters in 1946, four lighthouses finished, power generation down to 13.6 million kWh.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Mail extended to all countries on 14 January, postal savings re-registration under Korean names, 1,607 items of equipment ordered from Japan, JODK to resume 50-kilowatt output.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Rice collections at 78 percent of quota, 69,417 tons imported staples distributed in December, fertilizer through the Korean Agricultural Association, 43,900 tons coal allocated, price ceilings, 146,000 U.S. light bulbs.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Social affairs: refugee relief and repatriation, disease outbreaks, Winter Institute and Youth Movement, missionaries, information campaigns and press reaction to trusteeship, ending with a map of Korea.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: 183 relief boxes distributed, 4,624 refugee houses built, 10,036 Japanese repatriated from North Korea, smallpox vaccine output, typhus cases up to 647, typhoid 457, narcotics drive.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Four-week Winter Institute from 6 January, first Korean-language science textbook, Youth Movement with 19,270 members, scientists' conference of 30-31 January, returning missionaries.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Rice collection pamphlets and Mobile Education Train, 'Cholera' film, radio programs, newspaper reaction to the trusteeship resolution and Coalition Committee, plus map of Korea.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: Library due-date slip, blank digitization pages and rear cover of the University of Virginia copy.
